evidence: One inaccurate current-scope statement remains in criteria injected into a dimension prompt. Frozen task/tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:29 says "Revisions, Save conflicts, title validation, process-restart durability, sandbox enforcement and styling remain scored behavior." The current public contract instead defines titles as display names and separate record identities (environment/instructions/behaviour.md:25-29), while policy.md:5 leaves labels/API fields to the builder; no public note defines title-validation rules. The complete current Functional file contains 80 outcomes (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:23-581); its saved-record outcomes cover fidelity, durability, conflicts, immutable history, restore/retry and races, with no title-validation outcome. Thus the injected sentence incorrectly describes the current scoring scope. All other inspected product identity and surface statements agree: instruction.md:1, app_context.md:3-12, both gate prompts and all scored prompts describe a local no-sign-in JS/HTML playground with editor/preview/console and shared saved history, with no leftover account list or foreign product. The 22 protocol headers match Functional prompt.md:9. Source-only adversarial review considered a dead Run/localStorage-only mock (the explicit authored-Run/clean-context gates reject it) and a conforming app with alternative control labels, layouts and nonconsecutive revision identifiers (explicitly allowed by Functional prompt.md:11 and :463). The inaccurate title-validation sentence is a bounded editorial scope defect; no measured incorrect judge score is claimed. All 21 hashes in the current raw-evidence index matched; that index explicitly limits its observations to scripted product evidence and does not establish configured-judge behavior.
counterexample: A conforming playground preserves arbitrary display titles exactly, including repeated titles under separate identities, while satisfying all current 80 Functional outcomes. The Constraints prompt still tells its reviewer that title validation is a scored feature even though no such outcome or validation rule exists. Conversely a title-normalising implementation would not be tested by any title-validation-specific outcome despite that statement. The demonstrable failure here is the prompt's inaccurate scope claim, not a measured false app grade.
suggested_fix: Remove "title validation" from the Constraints criterion's deferred-behavior list so the injected prompt describes only the current scope; do not add a new product requirement to justify the residue.
